'''Jeffery Scott Swanagan''' (October 24, 1957 - June 28, 2009) was an American [[Executive director|director]] of several major [[aquariums]] and [[zoos]] in the [[United States]], including the [[Florida Aquarium]], [[Zoo Atlanta]], the [[Georgia Aquarium]], and the [[Columbus Zoo and Aquarium]].<ref name=sb>{{cite news|first=Margie |last=Trax Page |title=Geneva's aquarium expert dies |url=http://www.starbeacon.com/local/local_story_180235738.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130203082834/http://www.starbeacon.com/local/local_story_180235738.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2013-02-03 |work=[[Star Beacon]] |date=2009-06-29 |access-date=2009-07-12 }}</ref> He was the founding [[executive director]] and president of the Georgia Aquarium and is credited with much of the aquarium's creation and design.<ref name=ajc>{{cite news|first=Jim|last=Tharpe|title=Georgia Aquarium creator dies|url=http://www.ajc.com/services/content/printedition/2009/06/30/swanagan0630.html|work=[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=2009-06-30|access-date=2009-07-12|archive-date=2011-06-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604093329/http://www.ajc.com/services/content/printedition/2009/06/30/swanagan0630.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Swanagan and his family moved from [[Footville, Ohio]], to [[Geneva-on-the-Lake, Ohio]], in the early 1970s.<ref name=sb/> He attended [[Geneva High School (Ohio)|Geneva High School]] during his junior and senior year and graduated from the school in 1976 lettering in football.  Swanagan was a foreign exchange student in France during high school and was fluent in French.<ref name=sb/>

Swanagan attended [[Ohio State University]]<!--Wikipedians do not use "The" as part of Ohio State's name; it is considered a marketing gimmick, and routinely deleted.--> following graduation from high school. Later on, while working at [[Zoo Atlanta]], Swanagan earned his master's degree from the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]].

==Career==
Swanagan began his career when he joined the Columbus Zoo as an [[intern]] in 1980.<ref name=ajc2/>  The zoo's director, [[Jack Hanna]], met Swanagan in 1978 while he was working at a nearby hotel as an Ohio State University science education student.<ref name=spt/> OSU professor Dr. Barbara Thomson assigned Swanagan to the Columbus Zoo & Aquarium for a semester letter grade. Hanna hired Swanagan as a zookeeper two years later.<ref name=spt/>  In 1982, Hanna promoted Swanagan to the position of education director, a job that he held until 1987.<ref name=ajc2/>

Swanagan worked as the deputy director of Zoo Atlanta from 1992 until 1998.<ref name=sb/>

=== Florida Aquarium ===
{{main|Florida Aquarium}}
[[File:Florida aquarium exterior.jpg|left|thumb|230px|Florida Aquarium in Tampa]]
Swanagan departed Zoo Atlanta to serve as the [[CEO]] of the [[Florida Aquarium]] in [[Tampa]] from 1998 to 2002.<ref name=sb/> He was credited with rescuing the Florida Aquarium from heavy financial [[debt]] and poor attendance.<ref name=spt/>

The Florida Aquarium was constructed with borrowed money amid exaggerated attendance projections, according to the ''[[St. Petersburg Times]]''.<ref name=spt/> However, once the aquarium opened, attendance numbers were much lower than expected. Visitors often found the Florida Aquarium's heavy emphasis on [[Environment of Florida|Florida wildlife]] and [[science]] to be boring.<ref name=spt/>

The city of Tampa took over the ownership of the [[Mortgage loan|mortgage]] of the heavily indebted aquarium.<ref name=spt/> Aquarium [[managers]] demoted or [[laid off]] more than one-third of the aquarium's staff in response to the financial crisis.<ref name=spt/>

Swanagan reacted to the crisis by introducing new exhibits of animal life from outside Florida.<ref name=spt/> These exhibits included [[leafy sea dragon]]s, snakes, bats, and an albino [[alligator]], as well as a [[sting ray]], which marketers named Rosanne Barb.<ref name=spt/> Under Swanagan, the Florida Aquarium paid off approximately $3 million in debt by 2002.<ref name=spt/> Swanagan also cut the aquarium's annual [[subsidy]] from the city of Tampa from $1.1 million to $700,000.<ref name=spt/> Additionally, attendance rose from 545,000 visits per year to a then-record high of 620,000 visits in 2002.<ref name=spt/>

=== Georgia Aquarium ===
{{main|Georgia Aquarium}}
[[File:Male whale shark at Georgia Aquarium.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A [[whale shark]] at the Georgia Aquarium.]]
In 2002, [[Bernie Marcus]], a [[philanthropist]] and founder of Home Depot, requested a meeting with the Florida Aquarium's Swanagan.<ref name=spt/> Swanagan had hoped for a financial donation to the Florida Aquarium.<ref name=spt/> Instead, Marcus offered Swanagan a job as head of a new aquarium he was planning, which would become the future Georgia Aquarium.<ref name=spt/>

Marcus, the founder of the [[Georgia Aquarium]], hired Swanagan as the aquarium's first employee in 2002.<ref name=ajc/> Marcus had donated approximately $250 million for the establishment of the Georgia Aquarium.<ref name=spt>{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Huettel|title=Jeff Swanagan, who turned around Florida Aquarium, dies at 51|url=https://www.tampabay.com/news/business/article1014238.ece|work=[[St. Petersburg Times]]|date=2009-06-30|access-date=2009-07-12|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090702051239/http://www.tampabay.com/news/business/article1014238.ece|archive-date=2009-07-02}}</ref> The remaining $40 million came from corporations such as [[Coca-Cola]], [[Home Depot]], Georgia-Pacific, AirTran, Southern Companies, SunTrust Bank and AT&T.

Swanagan became the [[Atlanta]] institution's founding executive director and president.<ref name=ajc/> Swanagan helped to guide the Georgia Aquarium to its inception in 2002. He worked with the aquarium's biologists to design and stock the aquarium, which would open to the public in 2005.<ref name=ajc/> He was charged with everything from the design of the building to the [[logistical]] nightmare of [[import]]ing [[whale shark]]s, the largest fish in the world, from [[Taiwan]] to [[Atlanta, Georgia]] with the assistance of the UPS company.<ref name=ajc/>

In an example of his early work, in 2002 Swanagan and aquarium [[biologist]] [[Bruce Carlson (biologist)|Bruce Carlson]] observed the sunrise in the vacant lot that would become the Georgia Aquarium.<ref name=ajc/> The purpose of Swanagan's and Carlson's observation was to locate the spot for the future aquarium's [[coral reef]] tank.<ref name=ajc/> The coral reef exhibit, which would become the largest indoor reef in the United States, needed a large [[skylight (window)|skylight]] to provide light to the sensitive [[coral]], so locating the most light on the site was critical to Swanagan.<ref name=ajc/>

The Georgia Aquarium opened in 2005 with Swanagan as its first president and executive director. The aquarium eventually became the state's second most popular [[tourist attraction]], revitalizing parts of downtown Atlanta in the process.<ref name=ajc/> Swanagan and the aquarium sustained criticism early in its history when its two original whale sharks died after receiving a chemical bath to eliminate [[gill]] parasites.<ref name=ajc/>

Swanagan left the Georgia Aquarium for the Columbus Zoo in 2008.<ref name=ajc/> Anthony Godfrey replaced him as the CEO and president of the aquarium.<ref name=ajc/> Swanagan had hired Godfrey in 2004 as the Georgia Aquarium's [[chief financial officer]].<ref name=ajc/>

=== Columbus Zoo and Aquarium ===
{{main|Columbus Zoo and Aquarium}}
Swanagan joined the Columbus Zoo and Aquarium as executive director in 2008 at the invitation of Jack Hanna, the director [[emeritus]] of the Columbus Zoo and a personal friend and mentor.<ref name=ajc2>{{cite news|first=Mike|last=Morris|title=Former Georgia Aquarium director Jeff Swanagan dies|url=http://www.ajc.com/gwinnett/content/metro/atlanta/stories/2009/06/29/swanagan_aquarium.html|work=[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=2009-06-29|access-date=2009-07-12|archive-date=2009-08-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090828161413/http://www.ajc.com/gwinnett/content/metro/atlanta/stories/2009/06/29/swanagan_aquarium.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He helped to develop several major attractions at the Columbus Zoo, including Jungle Jack's Landing and Zoombezi Bay exhibits.<ref name=upi>{{cite news |first=Mike|last=Morris|title=Columbus Zoo head Swanagan dead at 51 |url=https://www.upi.com/Top_News/2009/06/29/Columbus-Zoo-head-Swanagan-dead-at-51/UPI-71621246294908/|work=[[United Press International|UPI]]|date=2009-06-29 |access-date=2009-07-12}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Swanagan had five children. Shortly after the opening of the Georgia Aquarium in 2005, Swanagan married his second wife, marketing executive Suzy Holley.<ref name=ajc/>

=== Death ===
Jeffery Scott Swanagan died at his home in [[Powell, Ohio]], on June 28, 2009, at the age of 51.<ref name=upi/> He suffered a possible heart attack while napping on his sofa after an afternoon of gardening.<ref name=upi/>

Bernie Marcus, founder of the Georgia Aquarium wrote, "He will always be remembered as a friend and a creator of the Georgia Aquarium."<ref name=ajc/>

Many of the zoo and aquarium world considered Swanagan a great leader and an extraordinary visionary whose mantra was "Touch the heart to teach the mind." {{Citation needed|date=August 2009}}
